title: True and firm
hookLine: after the Shema comes "true", affirming what was said
carry: more than a dozen words, all saying yes

lines: A FRIEND TELLS YOU SOMETHING BIG.
cards: A friend has just told you something big. When they finish, there's a beat of silence, and then you say: that's true. I believe you.
It changes what just happened. Their words are no longer only theirs; you've signed your name next to them. The Shema has just finished, three paragraphs from Deuteronomy and Numbers.
And before anyone takes a breath, the prayer book puts one word right on its heels, so close there isn't supposed to be a pause at all. True.

teach.h: THE LORD YOUR GOD IS TRUE.
teach.b: The Shema ends: I am the LORD your God. The next word is emet, true.
The Talmud, in tractate Berakhot, says not to pause between them. Tradition finds the pairing in the prophet Jeremiah. In the old Jewish translation: "But the LORD God is the true God."

teach.h: WORD AFTER WORD, ALL SAYING YES.
teach.b: So the end of the Shema and the first word after it make one sentence: the LORD your God is true. Then the morning blessing carries on: emet v'yatziv, true and firm. And it doesn't stop at two.

True and firm, established and lasting, right and faithful, beloved and cherished, delightful and pleasant, awesome and mighty, well-ordered and accepted, good and beautiful, is this word to us forever.
More than a dozen words, piled up, all saying yes. It's a very old prayer.

teach.h: SAID IN THE TEMPLE EACH MORNING.
teach.b: The Mishnah, in tractate Tamid, lists the words the priests said each morning in the Temple, and among them is emet v'yatziv.

The Talmud even says that someone who didn't say emet v'yatziv in the morning, and its evening partner, emet ve'emunah, true and faithful, hasn't fulfilled their duty. Why so much insistence on one word?
Because, in the prayer's order, hearing isn't the end. The Shema says hear. Then emet answers: I heard, and I hold it to be true.
That's the word's job here: not only saying the words, but standing behind them.

how: Right after the last words of the Shema, the prayer leader and congregation say emet, joining it without a pause, and the morning blessing Emet v'Yatziv follows; in the evening the parallel blessing is Emet ve'Emunah.

o: true and firm, the yes said right after the Shema
a blessing said over honest business dealings
the oath taken before giving testimony in court

emet v'yatziv was said in the Temple

games.q: the Shema's last words are: I am the LORD your God. what comes next?
o: the word true, with no pause.
games.why: emet, true, joined straight on, so the line reads: the LORD your God is true, echoing Jeremiah: the LORD God is the true God.

practice: Think of one thing you hold to be true deep down, not an opinion about the news but something you'd stand behind, and say it to yourself in one sentence. Then, quietly, out loud, say: true.
If doubt comes, let it come, and see what's still standing.
